problem_statement: When a JSON parser is set up over a buffer together with an explicit length but the buffer is not NUL-terminated (the bytes immediately after the length-delimited region are unrelated data), the parser does not respect the supplied length. It scans past the end of the supplied region: a value that runs to the end of the length-delimited buffer leaves the parser positioned beyond that length, and the bytes after it are read. As a result, parsing a value at the very end of a length-delimited, non-NUL-terminated buffer mis-parses or corrupts the parser state, and the integer and long accessors return values influenced by the trailing bytes rather than the number itself. Truncated inputs that cannot be valid (a literal, string, number, pair name or object cut off before completion) are accepted as well-formed rather than rejected as syntax errors. Separately, the keyword values true, false and null are recognized only when they are followed by a space, a comma or a closing bracket; the same value followed by a newline, a carriage return or a tab is rejected. Required behavior: every scan must stop at the supplied length; a value not fully contained within the supplied length, or with a wrong/extra suffix, must be reported as a syntax error; a complete value at the end of a length-delimited buffer must parse correctly; the integer and long accessors must reflect only the number's own characters; and true, false and null must be accepted before any JSON whitespace character.

superseded_statements.problem_statement: jsonparse_setup() takes a length, but the parser scans for a NUL byte or a delimiter instead of honouring the supplied length, so a value running to the end of a length-delimited buffer advances state->pos past it (and the literal comparison over-reads via an over-length strncmp; the atoi()/atol() accessors read a non-NUL-terminated buffer).

causal_chain: The affected test case sets up the parser over a length-delimited buffer padded with foreign bytes (e.g. 'x') after the supplied length and asserts that the parser's position and value bounds stay within the supplied length and that truncated values yield a syntax error; on the unfixed parser the scans run past the length into the padding and these assertions fail. Another case checks that keywords followed by newline, carriage return or tab are accepted; the unfixed parser recognizes them only before a space, comma or closing bracket, so the parse sequence fails. A further case parses a number at the very end of a non-NUL-terminated buffer padded with '9' and checks the integer and long accessors; on the unfixed parser these accessors read the trailing bytes and return a value other than the number. These are the fail-to-pass cases; the new test suite is the consumer that exercises them.

verification.reason: The statement is close but does not specify the public state invariants, setup initialization, and number fractional-part conversion behavior that the hidden tests require. These can be added without revealing the implementation.

problems.detail: The hidden tests inspect public parser state fields pos, vstart, vlen, error and depth, but the statement does not specify that these fields must remain valid within the supplied length after setup and after jsonparse_next, including on error, or that setup must initialize them.

The hidden tests require that a number's value span includes the full numeric token (including fractional digits) and that the integer/long accessors convert only the integer prefix, ignoring the fractional part; the original statement only says the accessors must reflect the number's own characters.
The hidden tests reject a truncated array as a syntax error, but the statement's list of truncated inputs omits arrays.

leak_check.leak_detail: The added phrases about jsonparse_setup initializing state->vstart and state->vlen and about whitespace being skipped when the parser advances to the next token are closer to implementation behavior than to a pure bug report, but they do not reveal a substantial algorithm or internal helper.
leak_check.suggested_statement: When a JSON parser is set up over a buffer together with an explicit length but the buffer is not NUL-terminated (the bytes immediately after the length-delimited region are unrelated data), the parser does not respect the supplied length. It scans past the end of the supplied region: a value that runs to the end of the length-delimited buffer leaves the parser positioned beyond that length, and the bytes after it are read. As a result, parsing a value at the very end of a length-delimited, non-NUL-terminated buffer mis-parses or corrupts the parser state, and the integer and long accessors return values influenced by the trailing bytes rather than the number itself. Truncated inputs that cannot be valid (a literal, string, number, pair name or object cut off before completion) are accepted as well-formed rather than rejected as syntax errors. Separately, the keyword values true, false and null are recognized only when they are followed by a space, a comma or a closing bracket; the same value followed by a newline, a carriage return or a tab is rejected. Required behavior: every scan must stop at the supplied length; a value not fully contained within the supplied length, or with a wrong/extra suffix, must be reported as a syntax error; a complete value at the end of a length-delimited buffer must parse correctly; the integer and long accessors must reflect only the number's own characters; and true, false and null must be accepted before any JSON whitespace character. The JSON whitespace characters are space, newline, carriage return and tab, and they must be treated as JSON whitespace; a value followed by any of them must be accepted. The public parser state must honor the supplied length: after any scan state->pos, state->vstart and state->vstart + state->vlen must be within the supplied buffer, with state->vlen non-negative. A complete value at the end of a length-delimited buffer must leave state->error equal to 0 and state->depth equal to 0. For a number, state->vlen must be the length of the number's own characters within the supplied buffer, and the integer and long accessors must return the integer part of the number (ignoring any fractional part) and must not be influenced by bytes after the supplied length or by an excessively long fractional part.
